transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Reed (Northbridge Head of ML Ops), Marcus Lee (Northbridge VP Eng), Priya Singh (Northbridge Security), Dylan Carter (Infra)

Summary:
Quick renewal touchpoint + discuss capacity upgrade (dedicated GPUs), adding EU-west as a served region, and contract extension timing. Agree to run benchmarks and then finalize pricing amendment.

---
[00:00] Jenna (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick roll call, we have Samir from infra side, Samir you with us?
[00:08] Samir (Redwood): Yep, here. Hi all.
[00:10] Olivia (Northbridge): Olivia here.
[00:12] Marcus (Northbridge): Marcus on.
[00:14] Priya (Northbridge): Priya here.
[00:16] Dylan (Northbridge): Dylan, hi.

[00:20] Jenna: Cool. The agenda is short: renewal timing, dedicated capacity options for your peak season, adding EU-west as a served region, and any security questions. We'll go through high-level then Samir will cover the benchmark plan.

[00:35] Marcus: Sounds good. Quick context — our current contract runs through end of October, and traffic spikes in Nov–Jan. We want to lock in capacity + add EU for some customers. Also want to discuss extending for 12 vs 24 months.

[00:50] Jenna: Got it. I pulled your usage — current hosted spend is around X tokens/month, with some burst to dedicated we estimated. We recommended a 4xA100 reserved pool to hit your 95p SLOs under expected QPS. Samir, want to jump in on the perf side?

[01:02] Samir: Yeah. So from the last POC logs we saw prefix reuse is high which helps. For the expansion to EU we have two options: spin up a dedicated pool in eu-west that mirrors your us-west pool, or use multi-region routing with a lower-resident cache and failover. Dedicated EU will add fixed monthly commit but gives lower tail latency and data residency.

[01:30] Olivia: For compliance we need EU data to stay in region for certain customers. So dedicated EU pool is preferable. What's the delta cost?

[01:38] Jenna: Ballpark, a dedicated 4xA100 pool in EU is roughly +28-35% on top of the US dedicated commit, depends on exact instance types and reserved term. If you go 24-month term we can discount another 10%. I'll send a precise sheet after the call.

[01:55] Priya: On the security side — we need SOC 2 and ISO docs, KMS integration details, audit log retention for 12 months, and confirmation that Redwood Private on VPC would be possible if required. Any of that doc-pack ready?

[02:10] Jenna: Yes — we have SOC 2 and ISO27001 PDFs, KMS integration guide, and an audit log FAQ. I'll drop those. Note that Redwood Private is an option if you require on-prem or customer-managed networking; that is a separate engagement.

[02:24] Jenna: Samir, benchmark plan?

[02:27] Samir: Plan is two-part: 1) dry run with synthetic load mirroring your distribution to verify latency tail with 4xA100; 2) a small production shadow run with real traffic routing for 48 hours in a canary region. We'll need a service account and sample prompt set plus expected QPS and concurrency. Expect to complete in about 7–10 days once we get access.

[02:50] Marcus: For QPS, we typically peak at 350 QPS with median sequence length ~220 tokens, 95p latency target 250ms. Does that sound achievable?

[03:02] Samir: With dedicated 4xA100 and prefix caching we should be in the 200–300ms range for 95p for gen models; embeddings flow different but similar. If you have heavy context-window recalc or long sequences there is tail risk. We'll validate in the run.

[03:18] Olivia: There was mention previously of quantization — would Redwood support an int8 profile for these models to lower cost? And any quality regression risk?

[03:28] Samir: Yep we support quantized variants; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles. There is regression risk, but we can run evals on your prompt set to measure delta. Usually for retrieval/semantic search int8 is fine; for LLM generation depends.

[03:44] Priya: Also need to confirm data retention — logs should be kept only per contract and we don't want model training on our data. Is that controlled?

[03:51] Jenna: Absolutely — we have options: no-training flag, and enterprise contracts include explicit clause that customer data is not used for model training. We'll include language in the amendment.

[04:05] Dylan: One more infra detail — when you say dedicated pool, is that single-tenant hardware or multi-tenant scheduler? We've seen other vendors advertise "dedicated" but it's noisy.

[04:18] Samir: Our Dedicated offering reserves physical GPU capacity and isolates network-level traffic; it's not noisy noisy. There are shared control plane components but compute is reserved. I'll put the infra isolation doc in the pack.

[04:32] Marcus: Pricing — if we expand EU and take 24 months, what's the committed monthly and do we get a true-up mechanism for unexpected growth?

[04:42] Jenna: Yes 24-month gives stronger discounts. We support quarterly true-ups and overage rates at a predictable unit price. For large variance we can include a negotiated burst bucket. I'll include an example amendment showing terms.

[04:56] Marcus: Great. On timeline — we want to have capacity locked before Oct 20 to ensure provisioning ahead of peak. Is that feasible?

[05:04] Jenna: If we start benchmarks this week and finalize pricing early next week, legal can run a quick amendment and we can hit Oct 15–20 provisioning. It's tight but doable.

[05:12] Olivia: On benchmarks, access — what credentials do you need? We prefer token-limited service account + IP allowlist.

[05:20] Samir: Service account with limited scope, IP allowlist for test runner, and sample prompt/trace CSV. We'll provide the runner instructions.

[05:30] Priya: About compliance — for EU we require where KMS is hosted. Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS in eu-west?

[05:38] Jenna: Yes, in Private deployments we do; in Dedicated hosted we support integration with customer KMS in many cases. I'll confirm the precise KMS flow for EU and include in the pack.

[05:47] Marcus: Competitors — just to be transparent, procurement is also talking to Anthropic and a few managed vendors. Their pricing is sometimes lower but we care about tail latency and reliability.

[05:58] Jenna: Understood. We can share recent latency reports and some anonymized benchmarks versus public models; that'll be part of the materials.

[06:08] Samir: One note — if you want faster provisioning for EU, we can initially run routing with a smaller cache in region and then flip to dedicated once sign-off done. That allows a soft-launch.

[06:20] Olivia: That might work for some customers. But for regulated ones we'll need EU-only.

[06:26] Jenna: OK. Recap and next steps: I'll send pricing + amendment draft; Samir will send benchmark plan and credential steps; Priya will share any policy doc constraints; Marcus provide QPS/SLO numbers; we'll aim to have the formal amendment by 2026-09-13 to start provisioning by Oct 15.

[06:46] Priya: Quick question — audit logs retention — can you set retention at the tenant level?

[06:51] Samir: Yes, tenant-level retention policy is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has defaults but can be adjusted under enterprise terms.

[06:59] Marcus: One last small thing — we have internal tools that call embeddings heavily, about 40% of token usage. If we shift embeddings to a different cheaper model via Redwood Optimize, is it seamless?

[07:12] Samir: We can route embeddings to a cheaper variant and we also provide automated reranking and quality checks. It's usually a config change and some evals.

[07:22] Jenna: Alright team, let's capture owners — action items in the doc. Any final questions?

[07:28] Olivia: No, that's it. Thanks.

[07:30] Jenna: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack today and target the benchmark next week.

[07:35] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional microstutters, some proper nouns transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), and a few speaker attribution overlaps.
